title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE CONSTITUTION DAY CELEBRATIONS ORGANISED BY THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
subtitle:
SYNERGY BETWEEN JUDICIAL INDEPENDENCE AND JUDICIAL ACCOUNTABILITY LENDS STRENGTH TO THE ROLE OF THE JUDICIARY: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU

TIMELY DELIVERY OF JUSTICE IS AN ESSENTIAL COMPONENT OF THE VERY CONCEPT OF JUSTICE: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU

GREATER EMPHASIS ON INCLUSIVITY AND MERIT WILL FURTHER STRENGTHEN OUR JUDICIARY: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 NOV 2026 7:43PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu, graced the Constitution Day Celebrations, being organised by the Supreme Court of India, in New Delhi today (November 26, 2026).
Speaking on the occasion, the President extended her greetings to the fellow citizens on Constitution Day. She said that on November 26, 1949, the people of India adopted their Constitution. In 2015, on the auspicious occasion of the 125th birth anniversary of the principal architect of our Constitution, Dr. Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar, it was decided to observe 'Constitution Day' annually on this date. It is a day to pay respectful tribute to the great architect of the Constitution and to the ideals enshrined within it.
The President said that the Supreme Court, High Courts, and the district and lower courts have made an invaluable contribution to the glorious journey of our Republic. Over the past decades, there have been unimaginable changes across many spheres of life. In particular, the influence of technology and media has become increasingly pervasive and profound. While adapting its role to changing circumstances and expectations, the judiciary has upheld and strengthened the fundamental ideals of justice. From time to time, the Indian judiciary has placed special emphasis on judicial accountability, thereby bringing to execution the ideals envisioned by the framers of the Constitution. The synergy between judicial independence and judicial accountability lends strength to the role of the judiciary.
The President said that the timely delivery of justice is an essential component of the very concept of justice. To ensure that justice is accessible in a timely manner, the judiciary is undertaking various initiatives such as simplifying procedures, leveraging technology, and establishing special courts. She noted that despite these efforts, the massive backlog of pending cases remains a significant challenge for our justice delivery system. She expressed confidence that this challenge will be addressed through the concerted efforts being made at every level of the judiciary.
The President said that not everyone possesses the resources required to access the High Courts or the Supreme Court. Our Constitution mandates the provision of justice on the basis of equal opportunity, which includes the facilitation of free legal aid. The objective of this mandate is to ensure that no citizen is denied the opportunity to seek justice due to economic constraints or any other form of hardship. The President emphasized that the true progress of a nation lies in ensuring that every citizen has an equal opportunity to thrive and succeed. She underscored the importance of providing every child with equal access to quality education.  It is also crucial to focus on the quality and reliability of legal representation available to the poor and marginalized sections of society. In this context, the District, State, and National Legal Services Authorities must intensify their efforts to ensure that justice reaches these vulnerable and disadvantaged groups.
The President said that empathy and ethics should be given as much importance as the study of laws in legal education in our country. She urged the leading lights in the lawyers’ community to present inspiring examples for young lawyers. She said that the young lawyers should see that excellence can be blended with empathy, and competence with compassion.
The President said that larger and more active participation of women in the Bench and Bar will help make our society more fair, just, equitable and inclusive. She highlighted that a woman’s perspective can add to inclusion, diversity and balance to judicial decision-making. She underlined the need to encourage greater participation by women as judges and lawyers. Greater emphasis on inclusivity and merit will further strengthen our judiciary.
The President noted that the Supreme Court has taken steps to promote access to justice by prioritising cases relating to specially abled persons, acid attack victims, senior citizens aged above 80 years and persons below the poverty line. She appreciated the steps taken for more effective case management and listing, promoting digital transformation, and encouraging amicable resolution of disputes. She expressed confidence that our judicial fraternity will continue to uphold the idealism with which the members of the Constituent Assembly framed the provisions on the judiciary.

title: Vice-President releases updated editions of Constitution of India in all 22 Scheduled Languages on Constitution Day
subtitle:
Constitution in all Scheduled Languages reflects the spirit of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat: Vice-President

India’s linguistic diversity is its strength; respect every language and celebrate every mother tongue: Vice-President

Access to Constitution in mother tongue empowers citizens and deepens democratic participation: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 NOV 2026 4:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today released the updated editions of the Constitution of India in all 22 Scheduled Languages at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, on the occasion of Constitution Day.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan released the updated editions of the Constitution of India in all 22 languages listed in the Eighth Schedule, at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi today on the occasion of Constitution Day.

Union Minister of State (I/C) for Law & Justice Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal and other dignitaries were present during the occasion. 

@arjunrammeghwal
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
November 26, 2026
Describing the occasion as a historic milestone in India’s democratic journey, the Vice-President said that making the Constitution available in all Scheduled Languages celebrates India’s linguistic diversity and democratic inclusiveness. He noted that access to the Constitution in one’s mother tongue would bring governance closer to citizens and enable them to better understand their constitutional rights, duties and values.
Paying tribute to Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, Chairman of the Drafting Committee, and other members of the Constituent Assembly, Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan said that the Constitution is not merely a legal framework but the living spirit of the nation. He appreciated the efforts of Union Minister of State for Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, and his team in taking the Constitution closer to the people.He said these efforts reflect the commitment to preserving India’s linguistic and cultural heritage.
He also highlighted the initiatives undertaken under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to preserve and promote India’s languages and knowledge traditions. He said that Initiatives such as Gyan Bharatam and Kashi Tamil Sangamam reflect the commitment to safeguarding India’s civilisational heritage and strengthening cultural bonds across regions.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan observed that India’s strength lies in its diversity and that languages are not merely mediums of communication but also carriers of culture, tradition and identity. Emphasising mutual respect for all Indian languages, he said that while every individual has a special attachment to their mother tongue, respecting the languages and mother tongues of others is equally important. He called upon citizens to celebrate their own mother tongues and embrace the rich linguistic diversity that makes India a harmonious nation.
Recalling the words of Mahakavi Subramania Bharati, he said that although India speaks many languages, its thoughts, aspirations and actions remain united in service of the nation. He added that the release of the Constitution in all 22 Scheduled Languages embodies the spirit of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat and will strengthen India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat@2047.
The Vice-President urged everyone to work with the guiding principle of Nation First – Rashtra Pratham, emphasising that a strong and united nation is essential for the preservation and flourishing of all its languages.
Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Law and Justice, Shri Dr.Rajiv Mani Secretary Legislative Department,and other  dignitaries were present on the occasion.
The Vice-President highlighted that making the Constitution accessible in every Indian language is a celebration of the country’s linguistic diversity, democratic inclusiveness and constitutional values. 

He emphasised that respecting and promoting all languages strengthens national unity and reflects the spirit of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat.

title: INDIA’S CONSTITUTION IS THE BEDROCK OF ITS DEMOCRACY, NATIONAL UNITY AND FUTURE PROGRESS: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
subtitle:
LOK SABHA SPEAKER CALLS UPON YOUTH TO EMBRACE CONSTITUTIONAL VALUES AND DISCHARGE THEIR DUTIES WITH PATRIOTISM, COMMITMENT AND DEDICATION

CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY’S DELIBERATIONS REFLECT INDIA’S ENDURING TRADITION OF DIALOGUE, DEBATE AND CONSENSUS-BUILDING: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

LOK SABHA SPEAKER URGES YOUNG PARTICIPANTS TO CARRY IDEALS OF THE CONSTITUTION AND SPIRIT OF TRANSFORMATION TO EVERY CORNER OF THE COUNTRY

LOK SABHA SPEAKER ADDRESSES STUDENTS ON THE OCCASION OF SAMVIDHAN DIWAS
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 NOV 2026 5:44PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla said today that the Constitution of India is not merely the supreme law of the land but the very foundation of the nation's democratic ethos, national unity and collective aspirations. It has guided the world's largest democracy through successive phases of transformation while preserving its unity amidst extraordinary diversity. Emphasising the enduring vision and foresight of the makers of the Constitution, he said that the Constitution had laid the foundations of a robust parliamentary democracy and continues to illuminate India's journey towards peace, prosperity and progress.
Addressing young participants at the historic Central Hall on the occasion of Samvidhan Diwas, Shri Birla called upon the youth to move beyond merely reading the Constitution and make its ideals an integral part of their thoughts, conduct and everyday lives. He underscored that the vitality of a democracy rests not only upon the rights guaranteed to its citizens but equally upon their willingness to fulfil their duties and responsibilities towards society and the nation.
Recalling the historic legacy of Samvidhan Sadan, Shri Birla observed that the building had witnessed defining chapters of India's freedom struggle and subsequently the momentous deliberations that gave shape to the destiny of independent India. The historic premises, he said, stand as a lasting testament to the sacrifices, convictions and visionary aspirations that shaped the Republic. He added that the Constitution, with its universal ideals and democratic principles, continues to serve as a guiding light not only for India but also for democratic societies across the world.
Reflecting upon the extraordinary journey of the Constituent Assembly, the Speaker said that its members deliberated for two years and eleven months, bringing together diverse viewpoints, engaging in extensive discussions and resolving complex questions through dialogue, reasoned debate and mutual understanding. Despite differences of opinion, the members demonstrated an exemplary spirit of accommodation and consensus, placing the larger interests of the nation above all other considerations. This remarkable exercise, he said, remains a shining testament to India's democratic temperament and its enduring tradition of collective decision-making.
Shri Birla observed that the Constitution had provided an enduring framework for safeguarding India's unity and integrity while celebrating its immense diversity of languages, dialects, religions, traditions and cultures. By enshrining the foundational principles of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, it has ensured a common constitutional identity for all citizens and created a shared vision for the nation's future. India's parliamentary democracy, he said, draws its strength and legitimacy from these constitutional ideals and the faith of its people in democratic institutions.
Elaborating upon the distinct yet complementary responsibilities of the three organs of the State, Shri Birla said that the Legislature serves as the voice of the people's aspirations and translates their expectations into laws and policies; the Executive gives effect to these policies through their implementation; and the Judiciary upholds the Constitution, safeguards the rights of citizens and ensures justice. Functioning within their respective constitutional domains, these institutions collectively strengthen the foundations of democratic governance and reinforce public confidence in the constitutional order.
Lok Sabha Speaker further observed that the framers of the Constitution had displayed exceptional wisdom and foresight by envisioning a framework that transcended the immediate challenges of their times and remained capable of guiding future generations through changing political, social and economic circumstances. He emphasised that Parliament and other democratic institutions must continue to serve as vibrant forums for public aspirations, diverse perspectives and constructive deliberations, where ideas are transformed into meaningful outcomes for the people.
Shri Birla said that India's youth represented the country's greatest strength and an immense reservoir of talent, enterprise, innovation and creativity. At a time when young Indians are making remarkable strides in science, technology and emerging fields of knowledge, their vision, energy and determination would play a pivotal role in shaping the nation's destiny and realising the resolve of a Viksit Bharat. He urged them to remain fully conscious of the rights and opportunities bestowed upon them by the Constitution while recognising that their responsibilities towards society and the nation were equally significant. He expressed confidence that a generation equipped with constitutional awareness, legal understanding and a strong commitment to public service would make an invaluable contribution to strengthening democratic institutions and deepening the roots of constitutional governance.
Appreciating the enthusiasm and commitment of the young participants, Shri Birla urged them to take the insights and experiences gained at Constitution House beyond its historic walls and carry the message of constitutional values to their respective States, educational institutions, workplaces and communities. He encouraged them to become ambassadors of the Constitution, inspiring fellow students and young citizens to understand its ideals, participate meaningfully in democratic processes and contribute to positive and transformative change. He particularly emphasised the importance of ensuring that the benefits of development, justice and opportunity reach every citizen, especially those at the last mile.
Concluding his address, the Speaker called upon the participants to make patriotism, dedication, hard work and a steadfast commitment to constitutional values the guiding principles of their lives. He urged them to leave Samvidhan Sadan with renewed enthusiasm, enriched perspectives and a firm resolve to read, understand and imbibe the Constitution in letter and spirit. The collective commitment of every citizen to constitutional ideals, he emphasised, would remain the cornerstone of a strong, inclusive, progressive and developed India.
संविधान दिवस के अवसर पर संविधान सदन के केंद्रीय कक्ष में आयोजित कार्यक्रम में देशभर से आए विद्यार्थियों एवं युवा प्रतिभागियों के साथ भारतीय संविधान की गौरवशाली यात्रा, उसके मूल आदर्शों और लोकतांत्रिक परंपराओं पर संवाद किया। 
संविधान किसी राष्ट्र का केवल विधिक दस्तावेज नहीं, बल्कि उसकी लोकतांत्रिक चेतना, सामूहिक संकल्प और उज्ज्वल भविष्य का आधार होता है।

भारत की भाषायी, धार्मिक और सांस्कृतिक विविधताओं के बीच हमारे संविधान ने राष्ट्र को एक साझा दृष्टि और दिशा प्रदान की है। संविधान सभा के सदस्यों ने दो वर्ष, ग्यारह महीने के गहन विचार-विमर्श, तर्क-वितर्क और सहमति-असहमति के बाद इस दूरदर्शी संविधान का निर्माण किया। संसद और विधानमंडल जनाकांक्षाओं को अभिव्यक्ति देते हैं, कार्यपालिका नीतियों एवं कानूनों का क्रियान्वयन करती है और न्यायपालिका नागरिकों के संवैधानिक अधिकारों की रक्षा करती है। यही संस्थागत संतुलन हमारे लोकतंत्र की आधारशिला है। नारी शक्ति वंदन अधिनियम, 2023 जैसे प्रयास लोकतांत्रिक संस्थाओं में महिलाओं की भागीदारी को और सशक्त बनाने की दिशा में महत्वपूर्ण हैं।

लोकतंत्र की वास्तविक शक्ति जागरूक, विवेकशील और कर्तव्यनिष्ठ नागरिकों में निहित है। युवाओं की नवाचार क्षमता, तकनीकी कौशल और राष्ट्र के प्रति समर्पण विकसित भारत की महत्वपूर्ण शक्ति हैं। प्रत्येक युवा अपने कार्यक्षेत्र में निष्ठा एवं परिश्रम से दायित्व निभाते हुए राष्ट्र निर्माण में योगदान दे सकता है। संविधान के आदर्शों की सार्थकता भी तभी है, जब वे हमारे विचारों और आचरण में प्रतिबिंबित हों।

विकसित भारत 2047 का स्वप्न आर्थिक एवं तकनीकी प्रगति के साथ गुणवत्तापूर्ण शिक्षा, बेहतर स्वास्थ्य, समयबद्ध न्याय और समान अवसरों की सुनिश्चितता में निहित है। संविधान की वास्तविक सार्थकता उसके मूल्यों को आत्मसात कर प्रत्येक नागरिक के जीवन में समानता, स्वतंत्रता, न्याय और बंधुत्व की अनुभूति सुनिश्चित करने में है।
संविधान दिवस पर हमारा संकल्प हो कि हम अपने अधिकारों के साथ कर्तव्यों और दायित्वों का भी पूरी निष्ठा से निर्वहन करते हुए लोकतांत्रिक भारत को और अधिक सशक्त बनाने में सहभागी बनें।

title: LOK SABHA SPEAKER PAYS TRIBUTES TO SHRI RABI RAY
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 NOV 2026 1:46PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Lok Sabha Speaker, Shri Om Birla, paid floral tributes to Shri Rabi Ray, former Speaker, Lok Sabha in Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan , on his birth anniversary, today.
Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri Harivansh; Members of Parliament and former Members paid tributes to Shri Ray on this occasion. Secretary-General, Lok Sabha, Shri Utpal Kumar Singh and Secretary- General, Rajya Sabha, Shri P. C. Mody also paid floral tributes to Shri Rabi Ray.
Shri Rabi Ray was born on 26 November 1926 at Bhanaragarh village in the Puri district of Odisha (then Orissa). He was elected to the Lok Sabha for the first time in 1967 (4th LS). Shri Ray also served as the Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare. Shri Rabi Ray served as the Speaker of the Ninth Lok Sabha and remained in office from 19 December 1989 to 09 July 1991.
The portrait of Shri Rabi Ray is placed in the Outer Lobby, Samvidhan Sadan and was unveiled by the then President of India, Shri Pranab Mukherjee, on 10 February, 2014.

ओडिशा की पावन धरा पर जन्मे श्री रवि राय जी ने छात्र जीवन से ही स्वतंत्रता, सामाजिक न्याय और समता के आदर्शों को अपने जीवन का ध्येय बनाया। तिरंगे के सम्मान में गिरफ्तारी से लेकर समाजवादी विचारधारा को जनमानस तक पहुँचाने तक उनकी जीवनयात्रा राष्ट्रहित और जनसेवा के प्रति अटूट समर्पण की परिचायक रही।

लोकसभा एवं राज्यसभा, दोनों सदनों में उनकी सक्रिय सहभागिता ने संसदीय विमर्श को नई गरिमा प्रदान की। स्वास्थ्य एवं परिवार कल्याण मंत्री के रूप में उन्होंने जनकल्याण के प्रति संवेदनशील दृष्टिकोण अपनाया, वहीं लोकसभा अध्यक्ष के रूप में निष्पक्षता, शालीनता और संसदीय परंपराओं के प्रति अपनी निष्ठा से लोकतांत्रिक संस्थाओं की प्रतिष्ठा को सुदृढ़ किया। शून्यकाल की सुव्यवस्थित व्यवस्था, विषय-सम्बंधी समितियों की स्थापना तथा दल-बदल विरोधी कानून के संदर्भ में उनके ऐतिहासिक निर्णय ने संसदीय कार्यप्रणाली को नई दिशा प्रदान की।

सक्रिय राजनीति से निवृत्त होने के पश्चात भी वे वंचितों के उत्थान, नैतिक राजनीति और जनजागरण के कार्यों में निरंतर संलग्न रहे। उनका संपूर्ण जीवन इस विचार का सशक्त प्रतिपादन करता है कि लोकतंत्र की वास्तविक शक्ति सत्ता में नहीं, बल्कि सिद्धांतों, सार्वजनिक जीवन की शुचिता और जनविश्वास में निहित होती है। श्री रवि राय जी की सेवा-साधना, संसदीय गरिमा और लोकहित के प्रति प्रतिबद्धता आने वाली पीढ़ियों के लिए सदैव प्रेरणास्रोत बनी रहेगी। उनकी पावन स्मृति को विनम्र नमन।

title: Prime Minister shares an article highlighting how the Constitution remains our timeless compass towards social justice and Viksit Bharat
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 NOV 2026 2:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:

“Indian basmati makes its mark from the US to the Middle East: Record rice production of 1551.54 lakh tonnes opens new avenues for global exports”: Shri Shivraj Singh

“Crop diversification is changing farmers’ fortunes: Moong, mustard and groundnut register new production records”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 NOV 2026 5:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, today released the final production estimates of major agricultural crops for 2025-26 and the first advance estimates for the 2026-27 kharif season, sharing the historic achievements of India’s agriculture sector. Addressing a press conference in Delhi, he said that, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the hard work of farmers, supported by the government’s policies and initiatives, had enabled India to secure the top position globally in the production of rice, pulses, jute, millets and spices. The country has recorded an all-time high foodgrain production of 3785.38 lakh tonnes in 2025-26. Further, despite serious weather-related challenges, including El Niño and a delay in the monsoon, kharif foodgrain production in 2026-27 is estimated at 1671.43 lakh metric tonnes. This is 97.67 lakh tonnes higher than the average production recorded over the previous five years, reflecting the resilience and determination of the country’s farmers.
India’s growing presence on the global agricultural stage and rising exports
Addressing the press conference, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that India was not only meeting its domestic food requirements but was also making a substantial contribution to feeding the world. In global agricultural rankings, India holds the first position in the production of rice, pulses, jute, millets and spices. It ranks second after China in wheat, cotton, groundnut, fruits and vegetables, and second after Brazil in sugarcane production. Expressing satisfaction over the country’s achievements, Shri Chouhan said that India had adequate stocks of both rice and wheat. Indian rice was now making its mark across international markets, with exports registering a growth of 5 per cent. The aroma and quality of Indian basmati rice were reaching consumers across the world, including the United States, Canada and countries in the Middle East. He said that this growing global presence reflected the strength of Indian agriculture and the country’s ability to contribute to international food supplies while meeting its own requirements.
Focus on self-reliance in pulses and oilseeds, and on crop diversification
Union Agriculture Minister Shri Chouhan made it clear that, having achieved a surplus position in rice and wheat, the government’s focus was now firmly on crop diversification and making the country self-reliant in pulses and oilseeds. He said that domestic demand for pulses and edible oils was continuing to rise, making it important to increase production and reduce dependence on imports. To address this requirement, concerted efforts were being undertaken on a mission mode through the National Pulses Mission and National Oilseeds Mission. These initiatives are aimed at strengthening domestic production and meeting the country’s growing requirements. Shri Chouhan said that the positive impact of these efforts was now becoming evident in the final production figures, particularly in the improved output of pulses and oilseed crops. The emphasis on diversification would also help broaden the agricultural production base and support farmers in taking up a wider range of crops.
Final estimates for 2025-26: Historic records in foodgrains, pulses and oilseeds
According to the final estimates for 2025-26 released by Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, the country’s total foodgrain production has reached a record 3785.38 lakh tonnes. This represents an increase of 208.06 lakh tonnes over the production of 3577.32 lakh tonnes recorded in 2024-25. The increase marks a significant expansion in the country’s foodgrain output and reflects the contribution of farmers across different crop-growing regions.
Rice and wheat
: Total rice production has increased by 49.70 lakh tonnes from 1501.84 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 to a record 1551.54 lakh tonnes in 2025-26. Wheat production has also reached a historic level of 1220.64 lakh tonnes, registering an increase of 41.19 lakh tonnes over the 1179.45 lakh tonnes produced in 2024-25. These figures underline the continued strength of India's two major foodgrain crops and the country's capacity to maintain high levels of production.
Maize, Shri Anna (millets) and pulses
: Maize production has risen sharply from 434.09 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 to 550.25 lakh tonnes in 2025-26. Total production of nutri-cereals and coarse cereals stood at 740.80 lakh tonnes, of which ‘Shri Anna’ (millets) accounted for 172.09 lakh tonnes. Total pulse production increased by 15.57 lakh tonnes, from 256.83 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 to 272.40 lakh tonnes. Within this category, moong registered a new record of 43.96 lakh tonnes, while gram production stood at 125.13 lakh tonnes and tur (arhar) at 35.99 lakh tonnes. The increase across these crops highlights the contribution of diversification and the growing importance of pulses and millets in the country’s agricultural production.
Oilseeds and commercial crops
: Total oilseed production increased by 2.66 lakh tonnes over the previous year’s 429.89 lakh tonnes, reaching a record 432.55 lakh tonnes. Groundnut production reached a record 131.71 lakh tonnes, an increase of 12.29 lakh tonnes over the 119.42 lakh tonnes recorded in the previous year. Rapeseed and mustard production also reached a new high of 137.66 lakh tonnes, registering an increase of 10.99 lakh tonnes over the previous year's 126.67 lakh tonnes. Soybean production stood at 126.36 lakh tonnes. Among commercial crops, sugarcane production was recorded at 5037.29 lakh tonnes, cotton production at 280.06 lakh bales (each weighing 170 kg), and jute and mesta production at 94.28 lakh bales (each weighing 180 kg). The performance of groundnut and rapeseed and mustard, in particular, contributed to the record overall oilseed output.
First advance estimates for kharif 2026-27: Farmers’ determination overcomes the El Niño challenge
Releasing the first advance estimates for the 2026-27 kharif season, Union Agriculture Minister Shri Chouhan said that crop sowing had been affected this year by the return of El Niño, a delay in the monsoon during June, and rainfall that was 35 to 40 per cent below normal. Low soil moisture and drought-like conditions in major agricultural states such as Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh had also affected the sowing of crops including paddy, maize, tur, soybean and cotton. Despite these difficult conditions, the determination and resilience of farmers, the support provided through government schemes and the climate-resilient crop varieties developed by scientists had helped sustain agricultural production. Total kharif foodgrain production is estimated at 1671.43 lakh metric tonnes (LMT), which is 97.67 lakh tonnes higher than the average kharif production over the previous five years. Shri Chouhan said that this performance demonstrated the ability of farmers to overcome challenging weather conditions with the support of government initiatives and scientific advancements.
Estimates for major kharif crops
: Kharif rice production is estimated at 1219.05 lakh tonnes. Total production of nutri-cereals and coarse cereals is projected at 381.05 lakh tonnes. This includes 260.64 lakh tonnes of maize, 89.43 lakh tonnes of bajra, 14.79 lakh tonnes of jowar, 12.48 lakh tonnes of ragi and 3.71 lakh tonnes of small millets. These estimates provide an indication of the expected performance of the major cereal and millet crops during the kharif season, despite the unfavourable monsoon conditions experienced in several important agricultural regions.
Kharif pulses and oilseeds
: Total kharif pulse production is estimated at 71.32 lakh tonnes. This comprises 31.22 lakh tonnes of tur, 16.59 lakh tonnes of moong, 14.49 lakh tonnes of urad and 9.02 lakh tonnes of other pulses. Total kharif oilseed production is expected to reach 239.47 lakh tonnes. Of this, groundnut is estimated to account for 111.68 lakh tonnes and soybean for 102.44 lakh tonnes. The estimates for other oilseeds include 18.97 lakh tonnes of castor, 4.91 lakh tonnes of sesame, 1.17 lakh tonnes of sunflower and 0.30 lakh tonnes of niger seed. These figures reflect the expected contribution of pulses and oilseeds to kharif production and the continuing importance of these crops in the effort to strengthen domestic self-reliance.
Kharif commercial crops
: According to the first advance estimates, sugarcane production during the kharif season is projected at 4543.39 lakh tonnes. Cotton production is estimated at 248.66 lakh bales, with each bale weighing 170 kg, while jute and mesta production is expected to reach 97.06 lakh bales, with each bale weighing 180 kg. These estimates cover the major commercial crops for the season and provide an assessment of their expected production based on the information currently available.
Estimates prepared through digital crop surveys and three-tier scientific validation
Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan explained that the figures released for the 2026-27 kharif season were preliminary estimates. They would be revised in the second and final estimates after actual yield data became available from crop-cutting experiments (CCEs) conducted at the time of harvesting. The estimates for both years have been prepared using information received from states and Union Territories, along with inputs from remote sensing, the weekly Crop Weather Watch Group (CWWG), the Digital Crop Survey and the Digital General Crop Estimation Survey. Consultations were also held with representatives of the industry. The data underwent a three-tier process of validation and triangulation to assess and verify the information before the estimates were finalised. This combination of state-level inputs, digital surveys, scientific assessment and verification processes has been used to prepare the production estimates for the two agricultural years.

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across city route of Una, Mandi, Joginder Nagar and highway route of Una to Mandi and Mandi to Una under HP LSA, during the month of Sep 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.
These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc.  In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analyzed in real-time using advanced Software Systems.
TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across City drive – 373 Km, Hotspot locations - 06, Walk Test - 5.2 Km, Highway Drive – 225.1 Km, and Inter Operator Calling at 01 location during 15th Sep 2026 to 18th Sep 2026 in HP LSA
.
These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Delhi. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area / route under test on the day / time of conducting the drive test.

title: Three Antiquities Repatriated from USA and Netherlands Handed Over to Tamil Nadu Police by ASI
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 NOV 2026 7:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant step towards the recovery and restitution of India’s cultural heritage, the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) today handed over three repatriated antiquities to the Idol Wing CID, Tamil Nadu Police, at Dharohar Bhawan, New Delhi.
The antiquities, comprising two bronze idols from the Smithsonian Museum, USA, and one bronze idol from The Hague, Netherlands, were formally handed over to the respective police officials by the ASI.
The antiquities include:
1. Saint Sundarar with Paravai Nachiyar:
A 16th-century bronze idol belonging to the Vijayanagara period was photographed in 1956 at the Shiva Temple, Sri Narisvara, Viracholapuram, Kallakurichi Taluk, Tamil Nadu. It was repatriated from the Smithsonian Museum, USA.
2. Saint Kannappa Nayanar:
This Chola-period bronze idol from Arulmigu Agneeswarasamy Temple, Thirupugalur, Nagapattinam district, Tamil Nadu, depicts the Shaivite saint in a tribhanga standing posture, with his right hand raised towards his eye. It was repatriated from The Hague, Netherlands.
3. Somaskanda (Shiva and Uma):
This 12th-century Chola-period bronze idol was photographed in 1959 at Siva Temple, Sri Visvanatha, Alattur, Mannargudi Taluk, Thanjavur district, Tamil Nadu. It was repatriated from the Smithsonian Museum, USA.
The formal handover was undertaken by Shri Yadubir Singh Rawat, Director-General, Archaeological Survey of India along with other ASI representatives.
The restitution of these antiquities marks an important milestone in India’s ongoing efforts to bring its cultural treasures back to their rightful home. ASI continues to work towards the identification, recovery and repatriation of India’s lost heritage in coordination with national and international agencies.

title: Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat Attends Closing Programme of Observance of 350th Shaheedi Diwas of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji
subtitle:

Shabad Kirtan, exhibition and short film presented as part of the closing ceremony at CCRT Campus, Dwarka, New Delhi
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:

content:
The Ministry of Culture organised the closing programme of the year-long observance of the 350th Shaheedi Diwas of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji at the Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT) Campus, Dwarka, New Delhi. The programme commemorated the supreme martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji for the freedom of conscience, religious freedom and the welfare of humanity.
The year-long commemoration of the 350th Shaheedi Diwas of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji was observed from 24 November 2025 to 24 November 2026. Inaugurated by the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi at Kurukshetra, Haryana, the commemoration marked the beginning of a series of programmes across the country to highlight Guru Sahib's life, teachings and supreme martyrdom. As part of the commemoration, a commemorative coin and postage stamp were also released in honour of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji.
The closing ceremony was graced by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, who attended as the Chief Guest. Shri Iqbal Singh Lalpura, Former Chairman, National Commission for Minorities, and Shri Amar Preet Singh, Former Chief of the Air Staff, Indian Air Force, were the Guests of Honour. Senior officials of the Ministry and other distinguished dignitaries were also present on the occasion.
The programme featured Shabad Kirtan, an exhibition and a short film highlighting the life, teachings and supreme martyrdom of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji. These presentations provided an opportunity to reflect on his message of compassion, courage, human dignity and respect for freedom of conscience.
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said that the occasion marked not merely the conclusion of a programme, but the culmination of a year-long campaign of remembrance, reverence, reflection and public awareness dedicated to Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji. He emphasised that the purpose of the observance was to draw inspiration from Guru Sahib's life and teachings and enable the present generation to understand, adopt and carry forward his ideals.
He further emphasised that human achievement cannot be measured only through material accomplishments. The true purpose of human life and progress is to build a society where the freedom and dignity of every individual are protected and upheld. He said that the teachings of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji continue to guide society towards these values and remain relevant for generations to come.
Shri Amar Preet Singh, Former Chief of the Air Staff, Indian Air Force, highlighted that Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji dedicated his entire life to protect the rights and freedom of belief of others. He observed that while individuals generally strive to safeguard their own faith and beliefs, Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji devoted his life to protecting the beliefs and freedom of others. He noted that this makes Guru Ji's martyrdom truly extraordinary and an enduring example of selflessness and courage.
Shri Iqbal Singh Lalpura, Former Chairman, National Commission for Minorities, appreciated the efforts of the Ministry of Culture in organising the year-long observance and taking the teachings of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji to people across the country.
Shri Samar Nanda, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Culture, spoke about the various programmes organised by the Ministry across different states to take the life, teachings and philosophy of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji to people across the country. He highlighted how these programmes brought scholars, artists, religious organisations and local communities together on a common platform to share and reflect on Guru Sahib's ideals.
He further informed that the Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT) organised educational and cultural programmes in schools to engage students with the life and teachings of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji. As part of this initiative, workshops were conducted in 220 schools, with the participation of around 68,000 students. These efforts were aimed at introducing the younger generation to Guru Sahib's message of compassion, selflessness, fearlessness, service and the welfare of all.
Through these initiatives, the Ministry of Culture reaffirmed its commitment to preserving and promoting India's rich spiritual and cultural heritage and taking the timeless teachings of great spiritual leaders to future generations.

The meeting was co-chaired by Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh from the Indian side and Under Secretary, Ministry of Defence, UAE Lieutenant General Ibrahim Nasser M. Al Alawi.

Both sides agreed to enhance bilateral defence ties under a wide range of areas, specifically defence industry, defence innovation & advanced technology, artificial intelligence, cyber, military training and maritime safety.​​ They agreed to accelerate co-development and co-production partnerships in next generation defence equipment.

The Indian delegation comprised representatives from the Department of Defence, Indian Defence Forces, National Security Council Secretariat and Ministry of External Affairs.
To facilitate business-to-business (B2B) partnerships, a delegation from the Indian defence industry also accompanied the JDCC delegation. A B2B interaction between defence industries of the two countries was held on the sidelines of the meeting. The Indian defence industry delegation visited Tawazun Industrial Park and held a meeting with the Tawazun Economic Council, UAE, to explore potential areas of mutual cooperation with their UAE counterparts.
The Indian delegation, led by the Defence Secretary, also called on Minister of State for Defence Affairs, UAE Mr Mohamed bin Mubarak Fadhel Al Mazrouei. The two dignitaries exchanged views on the emerging geopolitical situation in the Gulf & West Asia region, and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the Strategic Defence Partnership. The Defence Secretary conveyed greetings from Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh.
Earlier, the Defence Secretary paid solemn tributes at Wahat Al Karama, Abu Dhabi, dedicated to the courageous soldiers who sacrificed their lives in the service of the UAE.

title: Raksha Mantri addresses Convocation & Valedictory Ceremony of 66th NDC Course in New Delhi
subtitle: Preparing for future security challenges while responding to immediate threats need of the hour amid evolving geopolitical dynamics: Shri Rajnath Singh
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 NOV 2026 2:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called for anticipating emerging risks, examining alternative scenarios and preparing institutions for the security environment of the future, while ensuring an effective response to immediate threats arising from evolving geopolitical dynamics and the changing nature of warfare. Addressing the Convocation & Valedictory Ceremony of the 66th National Defence College (NDC) Course in New Delhi on November 26, 2026, he asserted that the evolving global balance of power, emergence of new centres of strategic influence and recalibration of traditional alliances, coupled with the changing nature of conflict, have made the security environment increasingly complex.
Raksha Mantri added that conventional military threats are increasingly co-existing with cyber-attacks, disinformation, economic coercion, disruptions to supply chains and other forms of hybrid warfare, blurring the boundaries between internal and external security, and peace & conflict. He emphasised that India's geographical location, extensive land borders, maritime interests and growing international responsibilities place it in a complex strategic environment, necessitating a forward-looking approach to national security.
Stressing the need to connect strategic learning with national security policymaking, Shri Rajnath Singh said NDC provides a valuable platform to harness the collective professional experience and intellectual capabilities of senior officers from the Defence Forces, Civil Services and friendly countries. He pitched for greater utilisation of this intellectual capital to contribute directly to India's national security policymaking.
Raksha Mantri suggested that NDC, in consultation with the Ministry of Defence, institutionalise a mechanism to identify a few significant contemporary national security challenges for intensive examination during every course. These could relate to India's strategic neighbourhood, border management, maritime security, critical technologies, economic security, protection of critical infrastructure and evolving internal and external threats, he said.
Shri Rajnath Singh also urged NDC to develop a mechanism through which serving senior military officers, civil servants and other relevant authorities are invited to formally pose specific contemporary challenges confronting the nation for examination by the course participants. “The challenges could be drawn from actual operational, strategic, administrative and policy concerns being faced by different Ministries & organisations. This would bring real-world issues into the academic framework of NDC and provide an opportunity to examine them from multiple perspectives,” he said.
Underlining the need to translate academic research into actionable policy inputs, Raksha Mantri emphasised that research undertaken by course participants should not remain confined to academic papers or classroom discussions. He stressed that selected studies should culminate in comprehensive reports containing specific, practical and actionable recommendations. These, he said, should be formally submitted to the Ministry of Defence and other concerned Ministries, wherever relevant, and presented before appropriate levels of Government for consideration.
"Every course at NDC should leave behind not merely a graduating batch of trained strategic leaders, but also a body of research, analysis and policy recommendations that contributes to the nation’s institutional knowledge and national security preparedness. The intellectual capital generated at NDC should find meaningful expression in our strategic thinking and policymaking processes. Here, dynamic linkage is the key," said Shri Rajnath Singh.
Raksha Mantri stated that in the real world, particularly in matters of national security, leaders rarely have the luxury of complete information or the ability to examine every possible alternative before taking a decision. He emphasised that strategic leadership requires assessing available options and making well-considered decisions while remaining conscious of their wider operational, economic, diplomatic and institutional implications.
Shri Rajnath Singh called for further strengthening the Strategic Gaming Exercises at NDC by incorporating emerging technologies. These exercises should create more dynamic and realistic scenarios, facilitate the examination of alternative courses of action and enable participants to appreciate the wider and often unforeseen consequences of strategic choices, he said.
Describing NDC as India’s premier institution for strategic learning, Raksha Mantri highlighted that the College’s greatest strength lies in bringing together senior military officers, civilian officers and international participants on a common platform and providing them with a unique opportunity to explore not only cross-sectoral complexities, but also international perspectives. The diversity of experience and perspectives that this institution brings together is valuable in an era when national security challenges increasingly transcend institutional and geographical boundaries, he added.
Shri Rajnath Singh appreciated the introduction of specialised sessions at NDC on Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning, Robotics, Unmanned Autonomous Vehicles, Aerospace Technologies, Semiconductors and other emerging technologies. He also welcomed the introduction of a dedicated AI capsule and the incorporation of closed-loop AI concepts into Strategic Gaming Exercises. Such initiatives would enhance the contemporary relevance of the course and familiarise future strategic leaders with emerging technological developments, he said.
Raksha Mantri also acknowledged the academic transformation undertaken by NDC, stating that the Executive MBA in Strategic Leadership and Public Policy, under the aegis of IIT Madras, represents an important step towards enhancing the academic rigour and contemporary relevance of the course. The association with an institution of the stature of IIT Madras has brought valuable expertise in management, science and technology into the study of national security, he said.
Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted NDC’s contribution to strengthening India's international strategic engagement through the participation of officers from friendly countries. He noted that studying alongside Indian counterparts provides these officers opportunities for sustained professional interaction, appreciation of diverse strategic perspectives and the development of lasting bonds of friendship and mutual trust. Such relationships, built through shared learning and experience, become an enduring asset in India's engagement with partner countries.
Raksha Mantri also acknowledged the role of initiatives such as the International Strategic Engagement Programme (INSTEP) in facilitating wider international interaction. He referred to the recently concluded fourth edition of the two-week programme which brought together 25 international participants from 22 countries of the Global South, along with 10 senior officers from the Indian Defence Forces & Civil Services and three officers from defence companies.
Underscoring the importance of international cooperation in an increasingly interconnected world, Shri Rajnath Singh said: “India believes in a collaborative approach to addressing such challenges, based on respect for sovereignty, mutual trust and shared responsibilities. The professional relationships and friendships developed at NDC should continue well beyond the completion of the course. The institution’s international alumni network represents a valuable reservoir of experience and strategic understanding that can contribute to stronger bilateral relationships and international cooperation.”
Commandant, NDC Air Marshal Manish Kumar Gupta and Dean (Faculty), IIT Madras Prof K Murali, senior officials of the Ministry of Defence and faculty & participants of NDC course were present on the occasion.
About 66th NDC Course
The Course is run for 47 weeks from January to November every year, divided into six studies. These six studies are Understanding India & Introduction to Strategy, Study on Economic Security, Science and Technology, Global Issues, International Security Environment, India's Strategic Neighbourhood and Strategies & Structures for National Security.
A total of 122 officers attended the course including officers from India and abroad. They are drawn from the Indian Defence Forces, Indian Civil Services, Indian Police Services and other organs of the Government. 40 foreign officers were from Afghanistan, Australia, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Brazil, Egypt, Indonesia, Iran, Japan, Kenya, Kazakhstan, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Nigeria, Philippines, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Sri Lanka, UK, USA, Uzbekistan and Vietnam.

title: New approach to detecting solar particle events could expand the geographic coverage of ground-based observations
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 NOV 2026 4:36PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Indian research stations in the Arctic (Ny-Ålesund) and Antarctic (Maitri) regions through the gamma-ray detectors gamma-ray detectors installed in them have established a new approach to detecting rare and extreme solar events called Ground-Level Enhancement (GLE).
This study of GLEs which could expand the geographic coverage of ground-based observations and help improve understanding of the Sun–Earth connection and help in assessing the potential impacts of extreme space-weather conditions.
GLEs, generally associated with powerful solar eruptions, in which highly energetic particles, primarily protons, travel through interplanetary space and penetrate the Earth's atmosphere produce secondary particles of hadronic, mesonic and electromagnetic types.
They are among the most extreme manifestations of solar energetic particle (SEP) events and often produce intense solar flares and fast coronal mass ejections (CMEs).
Scientists at the Indian Institute of Geomagnetism (IIG), Mumbai, an Autonomous Institute of Department of Science and Technology (DST), have for the first time detected GLE signatures from records of the solar event of November 11, 2025, designated GLE #77, (associated with an intense X-class solar flare, a fast coronal mass ejection and a strong SEP events) using gamma-ray detectors installed at Indian research stations in both the Arctic (Ny-Ålesund) and Antarctic (Maitri).
Fig 1: NaI (Tl) scintillation detector
Fig 2
: Gamma-ray and Neutron variations from  Antarctica (top) and Arctic (bottom) on 11 November 2025.
The NaI(Tl) scintillation gamma-ray detectors at Maitri in Antarctica and Ny-Ålesund in the Arctic were installed by IIG, as part of its research programme to investigate cosmic-ray and space-weather-related phenomena through ground-based observations at polar latitudes.
This new approach of detecting GLEs establishes the potential of ground-based gamma-ray observations, a comparatively cost-effective approach to complement conventional neutron-monitor measurements.
Gamma-ray detectors are relatively compact and cost-effective compared to conventional neutron-monitor installations. A wider network of such detectors could complement existing monitoring systems, expand the geographic coverage of ground-based observations, and improve our understanding of high-energy solar particles and their interactions with Earth's atmosphere.
The study involved a systematic analysis of gamma-ray observations recorded by NaI(Tl) scintillation detectors installed at Maitri and Ny-Ålesund. Systematic analysis was carried out to distinguish the GLE related enhancement from a variety of probable sources including background terrestrial radioactivity, terrestrial gamma-ray flashes (TGF), and thunderstorm ground enhancements (TGEs) associated with lightning activity, extra-terrestrial sources such as gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), solar flares, and so on.
Prof. G. Vichare, Ms. P. Thakur, Mr. C. Selvaraj from IIG and Prof. N. Gopalswamy from NASA processed the recorded data to obtain gamma-ray count rates in different energy ranges, and the variations were examined relative to the pre-event background level, along with the GLE signature in the traditional neutron monitor network and GOES particle data in different energy ranges.
Fig 3: Solar flare recorded by GOES
The gamma-ray detectors at the two polar stations recorded distinct temporal signatures of the event.
A prompt response was observed at the Antarctic station Maitri, while a more gradual response was observed at the Arctic station Ny-Ålesund. The gamma-ray observations were found to be consistent with measurements from neutron monitors, the instruments traditionally used for detecting GLEs.
The observations published in the journal Astrophysical Journal Letters, provided an important opportunity to study how high-energy solar particles enter and interact with the Earth's atmosphere at different geographic locations and under different geomagnetic conditions.
A wider network of such detectors at strategically selected locations could enhance the spatial coverage of ground-based observations and contribute to improved understanding of high-energy solar particle events.
The installation and operation of gamma-ray detectors at Maitri, Antarctica, and Ny-Ålesund, Arctic, represent an important contribution by India to the international effort to understand extreme space-weather events.
The successful detection of GLE #77 at both polar stations demonstrates the scientific value of India's polar observational capabilities and opens new possibilities for developing a complementary global network of gamma-ray detectors for space-weather monitoring.

content:
The
Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)
, under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, and the
Department of Social Justice and Empowerment
, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, have exchanged a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen multilingual accessibility across the Department's digital platforms and services.
The
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed and exchanged
in the presence of
Dr. Virendra Kumar, Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment; Shri B. L. Verma, Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment; Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Department of Social Justice and Empowerment; and Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, Digital India BHASHINI Division
, along with senior officials and representatives of the participating organisations.
The collaboration will facilitate the integration of BHASHINI's AI-powered language technology services with
SAMAVESH (Single Access Mechanism for All Verticals of Empowerment & Social Harmony)
, the Department's unified digital gateway for schemes and services. The integration will support access to information and services in
more than 22 languages
, helping citizens and beneficiaries engage with government platforms in languages they understand. It will also facilitate technology-enabled services, including
document summarisation
, further strengthening the accessibility and usability of digital information.
Developed by the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, SAMAVESH brings together the Department's schemes, services and organisational portals through a single digital interface. The platform is designed to simplify access for citizens, beneficiaries and other stakeholders by consolidating information and services that were previously available across multiple portals. Its multilingual capabilities, supported by BHASHINI, will help address language barriers in accessing information on welfare schemes and government services.
The integration also supports the platform's AI-enabled assistance features, including
Samajik Sahayak
, a chatbot designed to provide information and assistance in more than 22 languages. By bringing language technology into the citizen-facing digital ecosystem, the collaboration will enable users from diverse linguistic backgrounds to access relevant information and navigate services more conveniently.
The MoU reflects a shared effort to extend the benefits of India's language technology ecosystem to the social welfare delivery framework. Through AI-powered translation, speech and other language services, BHASHINI will support the Department's efforts to make digital information more accessible, inclusive and responsive to the needs of citizens across the country.
Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, Digital India BHASHINI Division, said:
“Our vision is to ensure that language never becomes a barrier to accessing government information and services. BHASHINI is advancing multilingual AI through text, speech and video translation, while extending its reach to tribal and underserved languages. Our ongoing efforts include digitising tribal languages such as Bhili and low resource language like Mizo and bringing them into the digital ecosystem. Going forward, we aim to extend these capabilities to government reports, scheme documents and videos, while enabling speech accessibility across digital platforms. title: India AI Mission-supported Chariot-1 Foundation Models Launched, Strengthening India's Indigenous AI Capabilities
subtitle: Developed in India through Indigenous Research, Chariot-1 Advances Multilingual Language Processing and Speech Generation with Innovations Tailored to India's Linguistic Diversity
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 NOV 2026 11:23AM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant milestone towards strengthening India's indigenous Artificial Intelligence (AI) ecosystem, Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), inaugurated the launch of
Chariot-1 Foundation Models
, developed by Chariot Artificial Intelligence Pvt. Ltd., under the IndiaAI Mission. The launch and research showcase took place at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, highlighting India's growing capability to develop sovereign AI technologies through homegrown research and innovation.
Chariot Artificial Intelligence Pvt. Ltd. is among the first four teams selected under the IndiaAI Mission to develop sovereign foundation models. The initiative reflects the Government of India's commitment to nurturing indigenous AI capabilities, supporting advanced research and enabling the development of AI models that address India's unique technological, linguistic and societal requirements.
The Chariot-1 model suite comprises
Chariot-1 Large Language Model (LLM)
and
Chariot-1 Text-to-Speech (TTS)
, developed through pre-training from scratch in India. Designed to advance language understanding and speech generation, the models incorporate novel research innovations aimed at improving computational efficiency, multilingual capabilities and adaptability across different deployment environments.
Advancing Multilingual AI through Indigenous Research
A key highlight of the launch was the presentation of three research innovations developed by the Chariot team and integrated into the training of Chariot-1 models. These innovations address fundamental challenges in language processing and model training, particularly in the context of India's diverse linguistic landscape.
IndicShift
, an open-source innovation, introduces a shared alphabet for Indian scripts, enabling AI models to leverage similarities across languages rather than treating each script independently. Covering 1,012 characters across 12 Indian scripts through 350 letters, the approach achieves up to 2.5 times fewer tokens on Indian text compared to OpenAI's GPT tokeniser. The research also reports a 5% to 8% improvement in model performance on Indian languages on the same compute, while maintaining performance in English and code.
Nested Training
enables three complete model sizes to be trained simultaneously through a single training run and one set of weights. This innovation addresses the challenge of developing separate models for different computing environments, enabling deployment across data centres, laptops, smartphones and edge devices. The approach delivers a reported 62 % improvement in training speed compared to training the three model sizes separately.
The third innovation,
Mixture of Vocabularies
, optimises the model's word-selection process by dividing its vocabulary into 11 groups and scoring only the relevant group at a time. This approach reduces the number of vocabulary entries scored per word by 5.7 times and delivers a 38 % improvement in training speed on the same GPUs, with negligible change in model loss.
Chariot-1: Building AI for India's Multilingual Landscape
The Chariot-1 LLM is an 11-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, with 4 billion active parameters per token. Pre-trained from scratch in India, it is available in three model sizes-10.7 billion, 1.7 billion and 745 million parameters-catering to varying computational requirements and deployment environments.
Complementing the language model,
Chariot-1 TTS
is designed to generate speech in English and 10 Indian languages: Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Gujarati, Punjabi and Odia.
A distinctive capability of the speech model is its ability to understand context and determine how numbers, dates, currencies, units, URLs and abbreviations should be verbalised. This enables more natural and context-aware speech generation, addressing an important challenge in developing speech technologies for real-world applications.
The model recorded
over 97% verbalisation accuracy
on the Async TTS Pronunciation Benchmark, comprising 1,029 real-world sentences and 2,251 instances of non-standard text across 42 categories. It also achieved a Hindi character error rate of 7.60 % and an average character error rate of 6.47 % across nine other Indian languages, the lowest among the systems evaluated in the reported tests.
These developments demonstrate the importance of building language technologies that account for the complexities of Indian languages, supporting the broader objective of making AI more accessible and relevant across India's diverse linguistic communities.
Leadership Perspectives
Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, MeitY, congratulated the Chariot team on the launch of Chariot One, describing it as a significant achievement for India’s technology ecosystem. He highlighted the team’s innovative approach, efficient use of Indian-language representation and its contribution to advancing indigenous AI capabilities. He noted that the IndiaAI Mission was designed to nurture and support such talent, and appreciated the contribution of the two Stanford graduates who chose to return to India to build advanced AI technology. He said that Chariot One exemplifies the potential of India’s young innovators and demonstrates the country’s growing capability to develop cutting-edge technologies.
The launch of Chariot-1 underscores the growing role of Indian AI enterprises in advancing indigenous foundation model development. Through the IndiaAI Mission, the Government of India is fostering a robust ecosystem for AI research, innovation and development, with a focus on building domestic capabilities and reducing dependence on externally developed technologies.
By supporting teams developing sovereign foundation models, the IndiaAI Mission is enabling researchers, innovators and enterprises to pursue ambitious AI research and translate it into homegrown technological solutions. Such initiatives are central to India's vision of building an inclusive, self-reliant and globally competitive AI ecosystem.
The event also featured a fireside conversation between Shri Vishal Dhupar, Managing Director, South Asia, NVIDIA, and Shri Suvrat Bhooshan, Co-Founder, Chariot, focusing on emerging developments in AI research and the evolving technology landscape.

ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

content:
The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India today commenced the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) Performance of Veterinary Services (PVS) Evaluation of India's Aquatic Animal Health Services (AAHS) with an orientation meeting held at the National Agricultural Science Complex, New Delhi. The mission marks an important milestone in India's efforts to strengthen aquatic animal health governance and align its systems with internationally recognized standards and best practices.
The orientation meeting was chaired by Gunjan Krishnan, Joint Secretary (Inland Fisheries), Department of Fisheries and WOAH National Focal Point for Aquatic Animals-India; Dr J. K. Jena, Deputy Director General (Fisheries Science), ICAR; K.C. Devasenapathi, Secretary, Coastal Aquaculture Authority; Ana Luisa da Silva Afonso, Team Leader of the WOAH PVS Mission; and K. Mohammed Koya, Fisheries Development Commissioner, Department of Fisheries, along with representatives from ICAR Fisheries Research Institutes, State Fisheries Departments, MPEDA, Export Inspection Council, FSSAI, BIS, the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying and other stakeholder organizations.
Addressing the gathering, Gunjan Krishnan highlighted India's vibrant fisheries and aquaculture sector and outlined the country's institutional, legislative and regulatory framework for aquatic animal health management. Ana Luisa da Silva Afonso emphasized that the evaluation would support India in identifying priorities and developing strategic plans consistent with WOAH standards and international good practices.
The orientation programme covered key dimensions of aquatic animal health governance, including research and development, disease surveillance, capacity building, trade facilitation, export quality assurance, food safety, regulatory compliance and standards relating to aquaculture inputs and feed.
The WOAH PVS Pathway is a globally recognized framework designed to support countries in assessing and strengthening Veterinary Services and Aquatic Animal Health Services through an evidence-based and independent evaluation process. The assessment examines four core areas: human, physical and financial resources; technical authority and capability; stakeholder engagement; and regulatory capability and market access.
As part of the mission, the WOAH expert team will undertake field visits to aquaculture farms, fisheries establishments, research institutes, aquatic animal disease diagnostic laboratories and quality control facilities across multiple States from 27 November to 9 December 2026.
The voluntary evaluation is expected to help identify priorities for capacity enhancement, targeted investments and institutional strengthening. It is also expected to contribute to improved disease prevention and surveillance, stronger collaboration under the One Health approach, enhanced confidence among trading partners and greater facilitation of international seafood trade.
The WOAH PVS Evaluation represents an important opportunity for India to further strengthen its aquatic animal health systems, support sustainable growth of the fisheries and aquaculture sector and reinforce its position as a responsible and globally competitive fisheries nation.

The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, celebrated National Milk Day 2026 on 26 November 2026 at Bapu Sabhagar, Patna, Bihar.
The celebration was graced by Shri Samrat Choudhary, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Bihar, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Panchayati Raj, Shri Nand Kishore Ram, Hon’ble Minister for Dairy, Fisheries and Animal Resources Department, Govt. of Bihar, Shri Pratyaya Amrit, Chief Secretary, Govt. of Bihar, Shri Naresh Pal Gangwar, Secretary (DAHD), Govt. of India, Ms. Varsha Joshi, Additional Secretary (DAHD), Govt. of India, Dr. Meenesh Shah, Chairman, NDDB along with other distinguished dignitaries from the Central and State Government.
In his address, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Bihar, Shri Samrat Choudhary highlighted the contribution of livestock farmers to rural development and the State's economy, he emphasised the Bihar Government's commitment to strengthening the dairy and animal husbandry sectors, enhancing farmers' income and contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. Hon’ble Chief Minister highlighted that Bihar currently produces approximately 48 lakh litres of milk per day and reiterated the State Government's target of increasing daily milk production to 1 crore litres.  Hon’ble Chief Minister congratulated the recipients of the National Gopal Ratna Awards for their invaluable contributions to transforming India’s dairy sector.
The Hon’ble Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan alias Lalan Singh highlighted that the India is currently leading the global dairy sector and contributes approximately one-fourth of the world's total milk production. Compared to 2013-14, the country's milk production has registered a significant increase of approximately 84%. India also ranks second globally in egg production and fourth in meat production. He also noted that milk production has increased from 7.19 million metric tonnes in 2013-14 to 13.76 million metric tonnes in 2025-26, registering a significant growth of approximately 91% in Bihar. Hon’ble Union Minister also highlighted the importance of the National Animal Disease Control Programme (NADCP), particularly the nationwide Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) vaccination programme, in protecting livestock health, preventing disease outbreaks and enhancing milk productivity and the achievements of the Rashtriya Gokul Mission, NPDD and other Central Government schemes in strengthening Bihar’s dairy cooperatives, livestock breeding and animal healthcare. He also appreciated COMFED for its significant growth, with daily milk procurement reaching 23.97 lakh kg and sales reaching 18.41 lakh litres. Hon’ble Union Minister reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to enhancing farmer’s income, empowering women, generating rural employment and promoting sustainable dairy development in Bihar.
On the occasion, the prestigious National Gopal Ratna Award, which is among the highest national recognitions in the livestock and dairy sector, was conferred to the awardees of National Gopal Ratna Award 2026. The awards recognised outstanding contributions towards the promotion and conservation of indigenous cattle and buffalo breeds, strengthening dairy development and enhancing livestock productivity. The awards were presented in three categories: Best Dairy Farmer Rearing Indigenous Cattle/Buffalo Breeds (Non-NER), Best Artificial Insemination
Technician (Non-NER) and Best Dairy Cooperative Society (DCS)/Milk Producer Company/Dairy Farmer Producer Organisation (Non-NER). Special Awards in each category were also conferred on winners from the North Eastern Region and Himalayan States.
Shri Naresh Pal Gangwar, Secretary, DAHD, Govt. of India, in his speech, paid tribute to Dr. Verghese Kurien on his birth anniversary, recalling his invaluable contribution to transforming India’s dairy sector, and congratulated all participants and awardees on the occasion of National Milk Day. He highlighted the breakthrough in Sex-Sorted Semen (SSS) technology as a significant step towards accelerating genetic improvement, enhancing cattle productivity and strengthening the dairy sector. He also emphasised on key central government initiatives of the sector.
The Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics (BAHS) 2026 was also released during the event, presenting comprehensive data on India's livestock sector based on the Integrated Sample Survey conducted from 1 March 2025 to 28 February 2026. The report provides estimates of milk, egg, meat and wool production in the country for 2025–26. According to the report, India's total milk production is estimated at 253.81 million tonnes, egg production at 156.88 billion numbers, and total meat production at 10.63 million tonnes. Out of the total meat production, poultry meat accounts for 5.13 million tonnes.
On this occasion, several important dairy infrastructure projects were inaugurated and dedicated to the nation during the event. These included key projects under the National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD), namely, the distribution of Data Processing and Milk Collection Units (DPMCU) sanctioned for Dairy Cooperative Societies; dedication of Mineral Mixture Plants at VPMU, Patna and TIMUL, Muzaffarpur; and dedication of the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) at Mithila Milk Union (MMU), Samastipur.
The event also witnessed the dedication to the nation of Namaste India’s 2 LLPD (2 lakh litres per day) Milk Processing Plant at Sikandarpur, Bihta, Patna, established with assistance under the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF). In addition, certificates were distributed for Veterinary Medicine Sales Centres sanctioned under the Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP), which further strengthened access to veterinary healthcare services.
A number of significant initiatives were also launched during the celebration. These included Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for Rating and Grading of Dairy Cooperatives and Milk Producer Organisations (MPOs), an Online Application Web Portal for the rating and grading process and Climate-Resilient Roadmap for India's Livestock and Dairy Sector towards Viksit Bharat @2047.
During the event, the Preamble of the Constitution of India was also read by all the participants to uphold the values of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.
A panel discussion with progressive dairy farmers was also conducted which helps in facilitating the exchange of experiences, best practices and innovations, highlighting their contributions to strengthening the dairy sector.
The occasion also marked the launch of Sudha Brand Makhana Kheer and Rabri and the distribution of Sudha brand sales outlet keys, aimed at promoting value-added dairy products and expanding market access for dairy products.
An exhibition was also organised to showcase the various dairy technologies, equipment, animal nutrition products, milk testing systems and dairy products. The exhibition highlighted innovations aimed at improving milk production, animal health, milk quality, operational efficiency and the overall development of the dairy sector.
The event witnessed nationwide participation from livestock farmers, milk federations, dairy cooperatives, and progressive dairy farmers, along with virtual participation from livestock farmers across the country.
The National Milk Day 2026 celebration provided an important platform to recognise the contributions of dairy farmers and stakeholders towards building a robust, inclusive and globally competitive livestock and dairy ecosystem and reaffirmed India's commitment to sustainable and inclusive growth in the dairy sector and to advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.
