title: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari Announces National Highway Projects Worth ₹75,000 Crore for West Bengal
subtitle: 22 National Highway projects worth over ₹8,700 crore inaugurated and foundation stones laid; ₹14,000-crore Kolkata Ring Road, Dankuni–Kolaghat Eight-Lane Corridor and Moregram–Kishanganj High-Speed Corridor among major announcements
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 NOV 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Road Transport & Highways Shri Nitin Gadkari today inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 22 National Highway projects worth more than ₹8,700 crore at Kolaghat, East Medinipur, West Bengal. The programme was attended by West Bengal Chief Minister Shri Suvendu Adhikari, State Public Works Minister Shri Ajay Kumar Poddar, Minister of State Shri Nadiyar Chandra Bauri, Members of Parliament, Members of the Legislative Assembly, public representatives and senior officials from the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH), National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and the State Government.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Gadkari announced a pipeline of road infrastructure projects worth approximately ₹75,000 crore for West Bengal, encompassing high-speed corridors, expressways, bridges, road widening and road safety improvements. Highlighting the role of infrastructure in economic and social development, he said that efficient road connectivity is essential for industrial growth, trade, agricultural development and tourism. It also facilitates investment, generates employment and improves people's access to markets, healthcare, education and other essential services.
The Minister stated that National Highway projects worth approximately ₹40,000 crore had been completed in West Bengal, while works worth around ₹35,000 crore were underway. He emphasised the need for timely land acquisition and necessary clearances to ensure the expeditious implementation of projects.
Two Major National Highway Projects Dedicated to the Nation
Two important National Highway projects were inaugurated and dedicated to the nation:
Palsit–Dankuni section of NH-19:
The 63.83-km stretch has been upgraded to six lanes. It will strengthen connectivity between Howrah, Hooghly and Burdwan, facilitate faster freight movement and support commercial activities along the Kolkata–Durgapur industrial corridor.
Four-lane bridge over the Ganga at Farakka:
Constructed at a cost of ₹521.20 crore, the bridge and its connecting roads will improve connectivity between Murshidabad and Malda, reduce travel time across the Ganga and facilitate movement towards North Bengal.
Foundation Stones Laid for 20 National Highway Projects
Foundation stones were laid for 20 projects aimed at improving road safety, strengthening bridge infrastructure and enhancing connectivity across the State.
Under the Road Safety Scheme,
57 Vehicle Underpasses (VUPs) and Light Vehicle Underpasses (LVUPs) on NH-12 and NH-19
will facilitate safer and smoother traffic movement. The Ramanagar Bypass on NH-116B will help ease congestion within the town, while road-widening and bypass works will reduce travel time and fuel consumption.
Under the Setubandhan Scheme, two major bridge projects at Norghat and over the Dwarkeshwar River will improve regional connectivity. These projects will strengthen access to tourism destinations such as Digha, Mandarmani, Tajpur and Bakkhali, supporting tourism and fisheries-related activities. Improved connectivity towards the Jharkhand border at the Gowai River check post will also facilitate interstate freight movement.
Collectively, these projects will improve connectivity between Kolkata, Krishnanagar, Baharampur, Malda and Durgapur.
Major Highway and Expressway Projects Announced
Among the major projects announced by Shri Gadkari are:
Kolkata Ring Road:
A 250-km Ring Road at an estimated cost of ₹14,000 crore. It will connect Kolkata with Howrah and North and South 24 Parganas and link Kona Expressway, Belgharia Expressway and Kalyani Expressway, providing an alternative route for long-distance traffic and helping ease congestion in Kolkata.
Dankuni–Kolaghat Eight-Lane Corridor:
A 58-km, eight-lane highway at an estimated cost of ₹20,000 crore. The project is expected to reduce travel time by approximately 1.5 hours for vehicles travelling from Kolkata towards Kharagpur, Balasore and Bhubaneswar and improve connectivity with Haldia Port.
Moregram–Kishanganj High-Speed Corridor:
A 245-km, four-lane corridor at an estimated cost of ₹12,000 crore, including a 91-km stretch in West Bengal with an investment of ₹4,500 crore. It will strengthen connectivity between NH-12 and NH-27 and improve access to border areas.
Barasat–Petrapole Highway:
A 75-km, four-lane highway at an estimated cost of ₹8,000 crore to improve connectivity between Barasat, Basirhat and Bangaon and strengthen cross-border connectivity with Bangladesh.
Belgharia Expressway:
A 7-km, six-lane elevated road at an estimated cost of ₹1,000 crore to improve connectivity to Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport and ease traffic pressure between North Kolkata and NH-19.
District Connectivity, Bridge Development and Road Widening
The Minister also announced several projects to strengthen connectivity across districts and improve access to important economic and tourism centres. These include:
A four-lane bridge over the Mayurakshi River in Birbhum district at an estimated cost of ₹1,000 crore.
A 15-km, four-lane road from Rampurhat to Sinchura at a cost of ₹875 crore.
Improvement of 34 km of NH-131A between Malda and Durgapur at a cost of ₹750 crore.
Construction of bridges and four-lane roads in Malbazar, Gurjan, Jhora, Mal and Neora in Jalpaiguri district at a cost of ₹375 crore.
A six-km, four-lane bridge over the Damodar River at a cost of ₹300 crore.
A bridge over the Mahananda River in Darjeeling district at a cost of ₹270 crore.
Widening of 47.55 km of roads between Telipara–Jumuar and Birpara–Falakata at a cost of ₹1,500 crore.
Widening of 106.61 km of NH-512 between Gazole and Hili at a cost of ₹3,000 crore.
Widening of 31.24 km of NH-117 (New NH-12) between Joka and Diamond Harbour at a cost of ₹1,000 crore.
Widening of 89 km of NH-116B between Nandakumar and Digha at a cost of ₹2,700 crore.
A 54-km road project between Namkhana and NH-12 at an estimated cost of ₹500 crore to ease congestion between Diamond Harbour and Namkhana and improve identified accident-prone locations.
Strengthening Road Safety and Interstate Connectivity
Shri Gadkari also announced improvement works at 59 identified black spots across West Bengal at an estimated cost of ₹5,100 crore. These include 25 locations in Malda, 20 in Nadia, nine in Jalpaiguri and five in Paschim Bardhaman. The proposed works include Vehicle Underpasses, Light Vehicle Underpasses and service roads to improve traffic movement and address accident-prone locations.
Highlighting the importance of interstate connectivity, the Minister referred to the 570-km, six-lane Gorakhpur–Siliguri Greenfield Highway, approved at an estimated cost of ₹38,000 crore, and the proposed Siliguri–Guwahati High-Speed Corridor, for which the Detailed Project Report has been completed. He also highlighted the Kharagpur–Bardhaman–Moregram Greenfield Expressway, Varanasi–Kolkata Greenfield Highway and proposed Raxaul–Haldia corridor, which will strengthen connectivity with Bihar, Jharkhand and important economic centres, including Haldia Port.
Shri Gadkari emphasised that the planned highway network would facilitate the movement of goods, improve access to industrial and agricultural centres, support tourism and create new economic opportunities.
Shri Nitin Gadkari appreciated the State Government in facilitating timely land acquisition, removing encroachment and necessary clearances for expeditious implementation of the projects in last 6 months and expecting the same continuous support in future projects also.
The initiatives will strengthen West Bengal's road infrastructure and its connectivity with neighbouring States, ports, airports, industrial centres and international borders, supporting trade, regional development and improved mobility for citizens.

title: Department of Land Resources Showcases Land Records Modernisation Initiatives to Sri Lankan Delegation

date:

content:
The Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Ministry of Rural Development, today hosted a delegation of civil servants from Sri Lanka visiting India under an exposure programme coordinated by the National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG). The interaction focused on India’s experience in digitising and modernising land records, with emphasis on the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP), computerisation of registration process, survey and re-survey, NAKSHA and Land Stack initiative implementation.
The Sri Lankan delegation was led by Ms. I.B. Gunawardhana, Additional Land Commissioner and Team Leader, and included Dr. A.P. Singh, Associate Professor and Course Coordinator, National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG) and Ms. G.D. Nadeeka, Land Commissioner along with senior officials from Sri Lanka’s land, survey and administrative services.
Welcoming the delegation, Shri Dilip Kumar, Secretary, Department of Land Resources, highlighted India’s efforts towards strengthening land governance through digital transformation, technology-driven reforms and integrated land information systems. He provided an overview of the Department’s key initiatives and schemes, emphasising the role of digitisation in enhancing transparency, improving service delivery and making land administration more efficient and citizen-centric.
“Digital transformation of land records is essential for transparent, efficient and citizen-centric land governance. Sharing our experiences and learning from one another helps strengthen institutional capacity and advance land administration reforms,” said Shri Dilip Kumar.
During the interaction, Shri Shyam Kumar, Director, Land Resources presented an overview of DILRMP and NAKSHA, highlighting key achievements, technological interventions and the progress made in land records modernisation, geospatial mapping and integration of land-related databases.
The interaction also covered the integration of property registration with land records through paperless registration and automated mutation, enabling electronic transmission of registration details to revenue authorities for timely updating of land records, reducing delays and manual intervention.
The delegation was also briefed on the Bharat Land Stack, an integrated GIS-based platform bringing together land records, geospatial data, property registration, zoning, building approvals, litigation and other land-related information to provide a unified digital view of land parcels.
The interaction facilitated the exchange of experiences on digital land governance and technology-driven reforms, highlighting opportunities for greater cooperation and knowledge-sharing between India and Sri Lanka.

content:
The CSIR-National Institute of Science Communication and Policy Research (CSIR-NIScPR), New Delhi, organised a three-day Skill Training Programme on “Artificial Intelligence for Libraries” from 17–19 November 2026 under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative (Phase III). The programme aimed to equip library and information science professionals, academicians, researchers, students and IT professionals with knowledge and practical skills in leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) for library services, research support, information discovery and knowledge management.
During the inaugural session, Shri Mukesh A. Pund, Head, Training Division, CSIR-NIScPR, introduced the objectives of the programme and highlighted the importance of capacity building in emerging technologies to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of library and information services. Shri Salim Ansari moderated the session.
The programme covered a range of topics, including the fundamentals of AI and its applications in libraries, chatbots and user interfaces, no-code web and app development, AI-based metadata extraction and smart cataloguing, research discovery and mapping, regional language translation, fact-checking, information integrity and the ethical use of AI.
A special session on “AI Tools for Research Support: Literature Search and Review, Summarising Papers and Checking AI Output Against Real Sources” was conducted on 18 November 2026 by guest faculty Dr. Ritesh Yaduwanshi, Assistant Professor, Indira Gandhi Delhi Technical University for Women (IGDTUW). The session introduced participants to AI tools for literature discovery, reviewing and summarising research papers, and verifying AI-generated information against authentic sources. It emphasised critical evaluation and responsible use of AI in academic and research activities.
The training highlighted the potential of AI in automating routine library tasks, improving information retrieval, facilitating intelligent knowledge discovery and enhancing user-oriented services. Sessions on smart cataloguing, metadata extraction, research mapping, chatbots and regional language translation demonstrated how emerging technologies can improve the organisation, accessibility and discoverability of information resources. Discussions on fact-checking and AI ethics underscored the importance of accuracy, transparency and human oversight.
The valedictory session was held on 19 November 2026, marking the successful completion of the programme. Participants were encouraged to apply the knowledge and skills acquired during the training to their professional practices and explore responsible integration of AI into library services.

title: Dr. Ambedkar Foundation Celebrates Constitution Day 2026; Reaffirms Commitment to Constitutional Values, Social Justice and Inclusive Democracy
subtitle:
Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar Highlights the Enduring Relevance of Babasaheb Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s Vision in Advancing Social Justice, Equality and Inclusive Development

Shri B L Verma, Shri Ramdas Athawale Pay Tributes To Bharat Ratna Dr B R Ambedkar for His Historical, Visionary Role, Contribution To The Nation

Former Chief Justice of India, Justice Uday Umesh Lalit Leads Reading of the Preamble to the Constitution

Delivers Constitution Day Lecture On ‘Constitutional Governance And The Legacy Of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’; Highlights The Significance Of The Preamble, Constitutional Uniqueness And Democratic Values

Academicians, Researchers, Students, Practitioners and Scholars Eulogize Dr Ambedkar’s Constitutional Philosophy And The Future Of Indian Democracy
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 NOV 2026 7:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Commemorating 77 years of the adoption of the Constitution of India, the Dr. Ambedkar Foundation (DAF), under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, celebrated Constitution Day at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC), in the National Capital here today, reaffirming the commitment to upholding constitutional values, advancing social justice and strengthening inclusive democracy.
The programme was organised on the theme
‘The Constitution @77: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s Constitutional Vision and the Future of Indian Democracy’,
paying tributes to the monumental contribution of Bharat Ratna Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly, in shaping the constitutional and democratic foundations of the country.
The celebration was graced by Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment and Chairman, Dr Ambedkar Foundation, Dr. Virendra Kumar, as the Chief Guest.
Union Ministers of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale and Shri B.L. Verma, and Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, were among the distinguished dignitaries present on the occasion.
A significant highlight of the programme was the reading of the
Preamble to the Constitution of India,
led by former Chief Justice of India, Justice Uday Umesh Lalit, followed by his special Constitution Day Lecture on
‘Constitutional Governance and the Legacy of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’.
In his address, Justice Lalit elaborated on the significance and utility of the Preamble as an expression of the fundamental philosophy, objectives and guiding principles of the Constitution. He explained how the Preamble provides an essential framework for understanding the constitutional vision and the values that must guide the institutions of the Republic.
Justice Lalit also highlighted the distinctive features of the Indian Constitution, its comprehensive character and its unique place among the constitutional systems of the Asian continent.
Tracing the early constitutional history of independent India, the former Chief Justice of India referred to the landmark judgment in
State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951)
, which examined the validity of the communal allocation of seats in educational institutions in the light of the fundamental rights guaranteed under Article 29(2) of the Constitution.
He elaborated on the subsequent constitutional developments, particularly the enactment of the
Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951
, which inserted Article 15(4), enabling the State to make special provisions for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes and Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Justice Lalit also drew attention to the institutional transition following the adoption of the Constitution, highlighting how the Constituent Assembly, in its legislative capacity, functioned as the Provisional Parliament until the first general elections based on universal adult franchise were held in 1951–52.
He explained that this formative period of constitutional development reflected India’s remarkable transition into a democratic Republic founded on the principles of popular sovereignty and equal political participation.
Emphasising that the Constitution is not merely a legal document or an instrument for the distribution of governmental powers, Justice Lalit described it as a living framework that sustains democratic governance and protects the rights and dignity of citizens.
He underscored the importance of constitutional morality, the rule of law and respect for democratic institutions in preserving the spirit of the Constitution, while highlighting the continuing relevance of
justice, liberty, equality and fraternity
as the guiding principles of the Indian Republic.
The address brought into focus the enduring significance of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s constitutional philosophy and his vision of a society founded upon social democracy, equal citizenship and human dignity for citizenry of the country. It also provided an opportunity to reflect upon the collective responsibility of constitutional institutions and citizens in preserving and strengthening the democratic foundations of the Republic.
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar emphasised the continuing relevance of Babasaheb Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s ideals in advancing social justice, equality and inclusive development, underscoring the importance of upholding constitutional principles in building an equitable and inclusive society.
Dr Kumar enjoined upon the younger generation to imbibe great principles and values enshrined in the Constitution for equitable, dignified and inclusive socio economic development of all the sections of citizenry in the country. He said the Constitution provides all the citizens the sense of pride, honour, dignity, equality and equitable opportunities to live an honourable, safe and prosperous life.
The Union Minister said the Hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s guiding principle of
‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas & Sabka Prayas’
gives sense of security and equality for inclusive socio economic development of all sections of people.
Union Ministers of State, Shri B L Verma and Shri Ramdas Athawale paid rich tributes to Dr B R Ambedkar for his historical and visionary role besides monumental contribution to the nation.
Shri B L Verma underscored the need to uphold all the golden ideals and commandments enshrined in the Constitution adding all sections of people deserve honour, dignity and equitable opportunities for inclusive development.
Shri Ramdas Athawale called for working for the protection and preservation of philosophy, objectives and guiding principles of the Constitution. He added that spirit of democracy, is the cornerstone of unity in diversity in the country.
Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, shared his perspective on the significance of constitutional values and the continuing efforts towards realising the ideals enshrined in the Constitution. He also urged people to imbibe the spirit of unique values and ideals in the Constitution and serve the people with sincerity and humanely.
Shri Rahul Kashyap, Secretary, National Commission for Safai Karamcharis (NCSK), Joint Secretaries MoSJE Shri Parveen Kumar Thind, Dr Sandeep R Rathod, Shailendra Kumar, Smt Monali P Dhakate; DDG Ms Pratima Gupta; Ms Nishtha Tiwari, CEO, DWBDNC ; Economic Adviser, Shri Rahees M, Director MoSJE, Shri Gaurav Singh Rajawat, Director DAF, Shri Vinesh Pachnanda and other senior officers and officials of the Ministry, were present on the occasion.
Deputy Secretary, Shri Kumar Nityananad conducted the proceedings.
The celebration witnessed the participation of Chair Professors, Assistant Professors and Doctoral Fellows associated with Dr. Ambedkar Chairs established in universities across the country, besides academicians, researchers, scholars, Law students, Law practitioners, senior officials and other distinguished invitees.
The participation of representatives of Dr. Ambedkar Chairs added an important academic dimension to the occasion, facilitating meaningful deliberations on constitutional governance, democratic institutions and the contemporary relevance of Dr. Ambedkar’s philosophy.
The programme also reinforced the role of these Chairs and academic institutions in promoting research, teaching, scholarship and dissemination of knowledge about the life, ideas and contributions of Babasaheb Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
The Constitution Day celebrations underscored the importance of sustained academic engagement, informed public discourse and greater constitutional awareness in ensuring that the Constitution continues to serve as a living instrument of social transformation and democratic progress.
Through the initiative, Dr. Ambedkar Foundation reaffirmed its commitment to carrying forward the vision and ideals of Babasaheb Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, strengthening constitutional values in public life and fostering a socially just, equitable and inclusive democratic society.

With the Trade Fair scheduled to conclude tomorrow November 27, 2026, the remaining days offer visitors an opportunity to experience India’s rich artistic traditions, purchase authentic indigenous products and support the livelihoods of artisans and entrepreneurs from diverse communities.
A Senior Official in the Ministry said that more than 130 artisans from 19 States are participating in the fair through the Ministry’s three Apex Corporations, namely the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC).
He said the participation of these Apex Corporations reflects the Ministry’s continued commitment to strengthening market linkages, promoting entrepreneurship and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for artisans and entrepreneurs belonging to Scheduled Castes, Backward Classes, Safai Mitras and De-Notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs).

‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas’
, aimed at fostering inclusive growth, economic empowerment and equitable development.
The pavilion features an extensive collection of traditional handlooms, intricately designed handicrafts, handcrafted jewellery, textiles, footwear, handmade articles and other indigenous products. These products represent the distinctive artistic identities, traditional skills and cultural diversity of different regions across the country, the Official said.
He said the growing consumer response underscores the importance of national-level exhibitions in enabling artisans to enhance the visibility of their products, interact directly with customers, understand evolving consumer preferences, establish business networks and explore new market opportunities.
The Official remarked that participation in a prestigious platform such as IITF also enables artisans to strengthen their entrepreneurial capabilities, expand their customer base and build sustainable business prospects, contributing towards greater economic self-reliance.
A significant highlight of the Ministry’s participation is the promotion of
TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme)
, which aims to establish a distinct market identity for artisan-made products and enhance their recognition among consumers, he said.
Through the TULIP initiative, the Ministry seeks to bridge the gap between traditional craftsmanship and contemporary market requirements, encourage innovation, strengthen entrepreneurial capabilities and create sustainable income-generating opportunities for artisans, he said.
The 45th India International Trade Fair 2026, inaugurated on November 13, has brought together producers, entrepreneurs, traders and consumers from across the country and abroad, providing a prominent platform for trade, commerce, entrepreneurship and cultural exchange.
As the Trade Fair approaches its conclusion, the Ministry’s pavilion continues to offer visitors an opportunity to celebrate India’s rich cultural heritage while contributing directly to the economic empowerment and sustainable livelihoods of traditional artisans.
The Ministry’s participation at IITF 2026 reinforces its commitment to promoting inclusive economic development, preserving traditional craftsmanship, strengthening grassroots entrepreneurship and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities towards the realisation of the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

Initially launched in 272 vulnerable districts, the Abhiyaan has subsequently expanded its coverage to all districts across the country, emerging as a nationwide people's movement against substance use, he added.

title: MoSPI launches State Dashboard on eSankhyiki to improve access to State-level statistics
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 NOV 2026 12:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Effective dissemination of official statistics requires that users can readily find the data they need, access them in usable formats and reuse them for analysis. The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) developed
eSankhyiki
as a one-stop window for official statistics. The portal enables users to search datasets, explore indicators through interactive visualisations, and consult the accompanying metadata. Users can access data through direct downloads in machine-readable formats and through Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), which allow data to be retrieved and used in other applications. Currently, the eSankhyiki portal hosts 43 statistical products with 1109 datasets comprising more than 139 million records.
The
Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research (VISTAR)
places emphasis on strengthening subnational statistics and expanding the use of digital tools across statistical processes, including dissemination. Through its Support for Statistical Strengthening component, the scheme seeks to strengthen the capacity of States and Union Territories to produce more granular statistics, including at the district level, and support their use in local planning and policymaking.
In keeping with this emphasis on subnational statistics and digital dissemination, MoSPI has launched the
State Dashboard
on the eSankhyiki portal. The dashboard brings together State-level data for selected indicators already available across statistical products on the portal. It has been developed in collaboration with the Institute for Competitiveness.
The dashboard currently presents
283 indicators of 21 statistical products across
10 broad themes
, including agriculture, education, work and wages, and gender and inclusion. Users can select a State and a theme to view the available indicators, or explore a theme across States. Interactive charts and filters support data exploration, while the accompanying metadata and statistical notes provide the context needed to interpret the figures. Users can also download the underlying data and metadata, and download or share visualisations. By bringing together indicators from multiple statistical products into coherent, theme-based State profiles, the State Dashboard strengthens the transition from data availability to effective data utilisation.
Through this initiative, MoSPI reiterates its commitment to strengthening the country's statistical ecosystem by leveraging technology and innovation to make official statistics more accessible, transparent, interoperable and useful for informed decision-making. The dashboard will be expanded progressively and additional indicators will be added. This forms part of the ongoing effort of MoSPI to improve access to subnational statistics for policy, planning and research.
The State Dashboard will be accessible through the eSankhyiki portal at
https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in

title: National Level Event on Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat to Mark Two Years of Nationwide Campaign Against Child Marriage on 27 November 2026
ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 NOV 2026 3:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Women and Child Development will organise a
National Level Event on Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat (BVMB) on 27 November 2026
, marking the second anniversary of the national campaign launched on 27 November 2024 to eliminate child marriage through a ‘whole of Government’ and ‘whole of Society’ approach.
The National Observance will be held at
Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi
, and will bring together representatives of States and Union Territories, Ministries and Departments, Child Marriage Prohibition Officers (CMPOs), Child Welfare Committee members, National Legal Service Authority (NALSA), civil society organisations and other stakeholders to reaffirm the collective commitment towards a Child Marriage Free India.
The National Level Event will be graced by Smt. Annpurna Devi, Union Minister of Women and Child Development, Smt. Rekha Gupta, Chief Minister of Delhi and Smt. Savitri Thakur, Minister of State for Women and Child Development.
The occasion will provide an opportunity to review progress under the BVMB Campaign, recognise the contribution of grassroots functionaries and stakeholders, showcase initiatives undertaken by States and Union Territories and strengthen efforts towards prevention of child marriage.
The observance assumes special significance as 27 November has been designated by the United Nations General Assembly as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage.
Since its launch, the Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat Campaign has focused on awareness generation, community mobilisation, strengthening the institutional mechanism of Child Marriage Prohibition Officers, encouraging timely reporting of cases and promoting the education, empowerment and well-being of girls. The campaign has witnessed extensive participation through awareness programmes, community outreach and pledge-taking initiatives across the country.
As part of the observance, States and Union Territories are being encouraged to undertake focused awareness and outreach activities at State, District, Block and village levels, involving Panchayati Raj Institutions, Urban Local Bodies, educational institutions, frontline functionaries, youth, community and religious leaders, civil society organisations and citizens. Special Gram Sabhas, awareness drives, pledge-taking activities and digital mobilisation are among the activities being encouraged to strengthen community-level action against child marriage.
The Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat Portal (
https://stopchildmarriage.wcd.gov.in/
) serves as a dedicated platform for reporting incidents of child marriage, accessing details of Child Marriage Prohibition Officers, recording awareness activities and taking the pledge against child marriage. Citizens and institutions are encouraged to participate in the campaign and take the pledge to make India free from child marriage through the Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat Portal, MyGov and MY Bharat platforms.
The National Observance on 27 November 2026 will reaffirm India's commitment to sustained, coordinated and community-driven action towards ending child marriage and ensuring a safe, healthy, educated and empowered childhood for every child.

title: The Return of the Spotted Sprint
subtitle: India’s Cheetah Population on the Rise
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                26 NOV 2026 11:14AM by PIB Delhi
content:
A Morning in the Undergrowth
The winter mornings at Kuno National Park begin in tranquillity, as sunlight spreads across its grasslands and scrub. Amid this landscape, a species that disappeared from India seven decades ago is gradually reclaiming its place. A joint Field team at Kuno, comprising Madhya Pradesh Forest Department and Wildlife Institute of India personal monitor the cheetahs through radio-collar signals, field signs and associated changes in their behaviour. Consecutively in October and November this year, these daily observations brought two special developments: the arrival of two new litters of cheetah cubs.
Each birth reflects years of planning, scientific management, veterinary care and dedicated fieldwork under
Project Cheetah.
More importantly, each new birth is an encouraging indication that these highly stress-sensitive animals are adapting to their new environment, establishing themselves and successfully navigating the challenges of life in the wild. It is a testament to their resilience and a promising sign of the growing ecological suitability of the landscape and the progress of India's cheetah reintroduction programme. Collectively, these developments mark another chapter in India's efforts to establish a viable cheetah population. They also signal the emergence of a new generation born and raised on Indian soil.  These new births also reemphasis India’s role in global metapopulations endeavours.
Also Read:
A Sprinting Revival: The Return of the Cheetah
A New Generation at Kuno
Kuno National Park, located in Sheopur district of Madhya Pradesh, lies in the northern part of the Vindhyachal mountain range. It has emerged as the principal site for India's cheetah reintroduction programme. The park recently witnessed two successive births, adding nine cubs to the country's growing cheetah population.
The first litter arrived in
5 October 2026
, when
KJP21
, a 32-month-old Indian-born female, gave birth to
five healthy cubs
. She became the third India-born female cheetah to reproduce, following
Mukhi
and
KGP12
. The cubs' father is a male cheetah brought from Botswana. Their birth therefore introduced the Botswana genetic lineage into country's India-born cheetah population.
This development holds particular significance under the
National Action Plan for Cheetah Introduction
in India. The plan identifies successful breeding by the first India-born generation, or F1 generation, as one of the milestone necessary for successful establishment of cheetahs in reintroduced sites.
KJP21's reproduction therefore marks an important step towards achieving this objective.
A second litter followed on
20 November 2026
, when
KOMG 3
, a 30-month-old female brought from Botswana, gave birth to
four healthy cubs
. Significantly, KOMG 3 became the
first female cheetah brought from Botswana to give birth in India
. She delivered her cubs in free ranging conditions after spending more than four months in the wild. This also marked the
second recorded instance of a cheetah giving birth in the wild
(outside of Closed Natural Ares (CNA), which are large protected/fenced acclimatization areas within the release sites) since the reintroduction programme began in 2022. Successful reproduction in the wild is another criterion identified in the National Action Plan for assessing achievements of the programme's long term goals. This also is a critical milestone for the global metapopulation initiatives as India offers space for breeding Cheetahs from the African Sub-continent which otherwise are fragmented.
With the arrival of the November litter,
India's cheetah population reached 62, including 43 cheetahs born cubs within the country
. India-born cheetahs now account for nearly 70% of the total population. This reflects the growing contribution of reproduction within India to the programme's population base. Altogether,
the two litters brought nine new cubs into India's cheetah population
. Their arrival marks an encouraging milestone, while their survival and future reproduction will remain important indicators of conservation progress.
From Reintroduction to Natural Reproduction
Where did our cheetahs go?
The cheetah officially went extinct in India in 1952.  The last confirmed sighting of wild cheetahs was recorded in 1947 in the Sal forests of present-day Koriya district, Chhattisgarh. The last three recorded wild Asiatic cheetahs in India were shot and killed in the Sal forests in December 1947. Thus, the nation lost the species once ranged from Punjab in the north to Tirunelveli in the south. India’s native Asiatic cheetah vanished due to a combination of excessive hunting, poaching, and the use of cheetahs for coursing. Large-scale habitat loss from agriculture, decline of prey, climate pressures, and the species’ low reproductive rate and narrow genetic base further accelerated their extinction. Project Cheetah is the first attempt anywhere to move a large carnivore between continents for reintroduction.
India’s cheetah story restarted with
Project Cheetah
on 17 September 2022 with a landmark release at Kuno National Park. On that day, the Prime Minister released eight cheetahs brought from Namibia into quarantine enclosures. Twelve more cheetahs arrived from South Africa in February 2023, completing a founder stock of twenty animals. The exercise remains the
world’s first intercontinental translocation
of a large wild carnivore anywhere. Project Cheetah is run by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change through the National Tiger Conservation Authority. Its stated aim is to restore the cheetah as a flagship species of open forests and grasslands.
The programme widened further on 28 February 2026, when nine cheetahs arrived from Botswana
. Six females and three males were released into quarantine enclosures at Kuno on that date. Each new source country adds genetic depth to a population that must sustain itself over many decades.
A Population Growing From Within
A reintroduction succeeds only when translocated animals settle into their new habitat and propogate there naturally. By that measure, India’s cheetah numbers are now growing largely through births on Indian soil.
Population propagation by cheetahs born in India has now become an important driver of this growth. This trend began in November 2025, when Mukhi, the first India-born cheetah under Project Cheetah, gave birth to five cubs. Two more India-born females, KGP12 and KJP21, have since followed her and given birth at Kuno. Their litters show that India-born cheetahs can mature and breed locally, completing a full reproductive cycle. This marks steady progress from the survival of individual animals towards a self-sustaining cheetah population in India.
Furthermore, each new breeding line matters because the founder populations of large carnivores usually carry a narrow genetic base. Sourcing animals from Namibia, South Africa and Botswana widens that base in a planned manner. A broader gene pool supports disease resistance, fertility and the long-term resilience of future generations.
The Science Behind the Recovery
Kuno National Park was selected following expert assessment of habitat suitability, prey availability and human disturbance. Earlier relocation of 24 villages, involving 1,545 families, made nearly 6,258 hectares available for wildlife conservation. These efforts helped reduce human pressures and create suitable habitat for cheetahs. Habitat management measures, including grassland restoration, prey augmentation and water management, support the reintroduction programme.
Project Cheetah follows a scientific framework informed by the
International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) guidelines
on conservation translocations. The
Action Plan for Introduction of Cheetah in India
was prepared jointly by the
Wildlife Institute of India (WII)
, the
National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)
and the
Madhya Pradesh Forest Department
. Monitoring combines satellite collars, camera traps and field observations. Distance sampling along fixed transects helps estimate prey abundance and assess habitat conditions. Veterinary teams monitor the cheetahs’ health, body condition, injuries and reproductive status.
Animals are first held in
Closed Natural Areas
before moving into the wider open landscape. This staged (soft-release) method allows each cheetah to adjust to terrain, prey and climate at its own pace.
Successful propagation further
indicates that cheetahs can reproduce under the conditions persistent at Kuno. However, reproduction alone does not establish that a population is self-sustaining. The survival of wild-born cubs remains an important measure of progress. The national action plan identifies cub survival beyond one year as an important milestone. Continued monitoring during this critical period helps assess survival, health and the programme’s longer-term prospects.
Grasslands, Prey and Local Communities
Under
Project Cheetah,
the cheetah has been designated a flagship and umbrella species for conservation. Protecting it requires the restoration of open forests, grasslands and semi-arid habitats. Kuno supports chital, sambar, nilgai, chinkara, chousingha, blackbuck and other wild ungulates. Chital is the most abundant wild prey and accounts for about three-quarters of recorded cheetah kills. Grassland recovery also improves soil stability, water retention and carbon storage across the wider landscape.
Communities living around Kuno are partners
in this effort rather than observers of it. More than
450 Cheetah Mitras
work as local ambassadors across 80 villages near the park. The programme has created about
380 direct jobs
, including trackers, patrol workers and trained guides. Villages around Kuno also receive a
five per cent share of eco-tourism revenue. Eco-development works
covering roads, check dams and sanitation extend across more than one hundred villages. Conservation gains are more durable when local communities share in the benefits they help generate.
The Road Ahead
The long-term objective is a self-sustaining metapopulation of
60 to 70 cheetahs by 2032
. This population is planned across about
17,000 square kilometres
in the Kuno and Gandhi Sagar landscape.
Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh has been developed as the second site under the programme. The first two cheetahs, named Prabash and Paavak, were moved there from Kuno National Park in April 2025. Subsequently, 2 females have also been shifted to the sanctuary.
A separate action plan guides prey recovery, habitat preparation and phased release at Gandhi Sagar. Additional habitats are being assessed so that the species is not confined to a single protected area.
As cheetah numbers grow, the programme is also spreading the animals across a wider landscape in Madhya Pradesh. In October 2026,
Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve
in Sagar district became the third cheetah habitat in the State. Two cheetahs from Kuno National Park were released there by the Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh.
The current total of 62 animals reaches the lower end of the planned range. It also includes very young cubs whose survival cannot yet be taken for granted. The nine cubs from the two recent litters are therefore an encouraging milestone rather than a final verdict. Their survival, and in time their own reproduction, will be the more meaningful measure of success. Each new litter brings India closer to a cheetah population that can sustain itself in the wild.

ministry: Office of Principal Scientific Advisor to GoI

content:
The third edition of the Technology Dialogue, themed
“Charting Technological Convergence,”
will be held from
30 November to 2 December 2026 at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru
. The Dialogue is being convened by the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, in partnership with the Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India
; Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru; Observer
Research Foundation (ORF); and Global Innovation Square (GIS).
Over the years, Technology Dialogue has emerged as one of India's premier Track 1.5 platforms for technology diplomacy, bringing together senior government officials, policymakers, researchers, industry leaders, investors, and innovators from India and across the world to deliberate on critical and emerging technologies and foster strategic partnerships. While the 2023 edition explored the opportunities and risks associated with disruptive technologies, the 2025 edition focused on technology diplomacy and India's strategic partnerships in critical and emerging technology domains.
Building on these discussions, the 2026 edition will focus on the growing convergence of frontier technologies across sectors and domains. The key domains in focus will be - Artificial Intelligence and Quantum Computing, Semiconductors, Bioeconomy, Neurotechnology, Cybersecurity and Post-Quantum Readiness, and Space Capabilities. As these technologies increasingly intersect, they are transforming global innovation ecosystems and creating new opportunities for scientific advancement, while raising important questions around economic competitiveness, national security, technology governance, and international cooperation. The Dialogue will examine how these technologies can integrate with national technology missions, eventually contributing towards building a globally competitive, resilient, and strategically autonomous innovation ecosystem.
The Dialogue will feature a distinguished and diverse group of thought leaders, including senior representatives from the Government of India and diplomatic missions, international agencies and multilateral institutions, and leading scientists, global technology companies, research organisations, venture capital firms, and deep-tech startups. Leaders and experts from several organisations alongside representatives from India's scientific and technology institutions, will bring perspectives spanning scientific research, industrial innovation, investment, policy, and international cooperation. Their participation will facilitate exchanges between those shaping technology policy, advancing frontier research, developing commercial applications, and financing emerging innovations.
Over the three days, the programme will feature high-level plenary sessions, expert panels, fireside conversations, closed-door policy roundtables, and curated walkthroughs of India's deep-tech and innovation ecosystem. Deliberations will explore the following thematic areas:
· AI x Quantum: Shaping the Future of Computational Intelligence
· Frontier Technologies Unlocking the Bioeconomy Century
· The Brain, the Next Frontier: Neurotechnology Augmenting Human Potential
· Beyond Cybersecurity: What it takes to secure the critical systems
· What and Who Will Determine Semiconductor Competitiveness in the Coming Decades
· Space 2050: Advancing Tech Frontiers for the Great Convergence
Complementing these domain-specific discussions, the Dialogue will address broader issues relating to deep-tech financing and commercialisation, access to advanced computing and foundation models, strategic technology partnerships, advancement in security technologies and responsible AI governance.
Dedicated engagements, including the India–Switzerland AI Policy Roundtable, organised in partnership with Swissnex as a satellite event under the
Road to Geneva
initiative, leading up to the Geneva AI Summit 2027, will provide opportunities to deepen bilateral technology cooperation. In parallel, a discussion on advances in security technologies will examine their readiness to protect critical infrastructure, identifying solutions that are ready for deployment and those that require further testing and validation.
Consultations on responsible industry behaviour in strategic AI will bring together policymakers, industry leaders, and technology practitioners to contribute to the evolving global discourse on technology governance. Complementing these policy engagements, curated visits to India's space, defence, and deep-tech innovation facilities will offer international delegates and stakeholders first-hand insights into India's emerging technological capabilities and their real-world applications.
A dedicated, activity-driven workshop in partnership with DSCI and GESDA will bring together national and international experts to demonstrate how technology foresight can be practised, moving beyond conceptual discussions to practical application. The workshop will introduce quantitative and qualitative methodological approaches and showcase how advanced digital tools, including artificial intelligence and machine learning, are enhancing foresight capabilities and informing strategic decision-making.
Hosted at IISc, one of India's foremost institutions for scientific research and innovation, the Dialogue seeks to strengthen strategic partnerships, foster cross-sectoral collaboration, and contribute to shaping the future of technology convergence, diplomacy, governance, and innovation.
Read more about the dialogue:
www.technologydialogue.in
